report.summary: compare_declared() marks truncated observations as 'agrees' even when missing columns may exist beyond MAX_NAMES (64). This silently masks CSV column mismatches for wide schemas, undermining the join between observed shapes and artifact schemas.

risks.finding: compare_declared() returns agrees=True for truncated shapes even if expected columns are missing outside the observed 64 names
risks.trigger: Comparing an observed DataFrame with >64 columns against declared names; if all observed columns match but a declared column is missing beyond the truncation, no mismatch is reported.
risks.location: shape.py, compare_declared: missing_in_observation=() when shape.truncated is True; agrees property uses only undeclared_in_observation

todos: Add a 'complete' flag to ShapeConflict and set agrees=False when comparison is partial due to truncation
Consider raising MAX_NAMES or making it configurable for wide-table use cases

handoff.suggestion: In compare_declared(), if truncated, set comparable=False with a reason, or introduce a separate partial_agrees indicator instead of silently hiding missing columns. Alternatively, always raise MAX_NAMES to a higher bound (e.g., 512) for table schemas, matching artifacts.py MAX_COLUMNS.
